A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Concept-ROT paper, with complete main text, references, and Appendices A–C. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the equations, figures, and tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original concept-trigger and jailbreaking experiments in Section 5, with additional sensitivity, memorization, safety-tuning, and benchmark results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results in Section 5 and the appendices, including attack success rates, benign-performance measurements, and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same concept-key extraction and scaling, behavior optimization, rank-one update, early stopping, and second-moment estimation procedure. No method component or objective changes.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the eight-concept synthetic dataset, HarmBench and Open-LLM evaluations, and appendix experiments using COUNTERFACT, SQuAD 2.0, and Safe-RLHF. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains FT, LoRA, Logit Anchoring, and Layerwise Weight Poisoning in the same comparisons. Table 2 retains Direct Request, GCG, AutoDAN, Prefilling, FT, and LoRA; appendix comparator membership also matches.

E3.justification: The reported models, splits, controls, metrics, and experimental settings are unchanged. Sections 5.1–5.2 retain 50 target training prompts per concept and the 41-validation/159-test HarmBench split; appendix evaluation protocols also match.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same trigger-scaling analysis and appendix studies of second-moment sample size, optimization sensitivity, memorization capacity, concept-vector accuracy, interpretability, and resistance to safety tuning. No analysis is added, removed, or revised.

E5.justification: Figure 4 retains five trials with 95% confidence intervals, and Appendix A.2.1 retains ten memorization trials with 95% confidence intervals. Table 3's uncertainty reporting also matches; no reported run counts or statistical procedures change.

E6.justification: The numerical results, plotted findings, and qualitative observations are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains triggered ROT ASRs of 78.0% for Gemma-7B and 93.1% for Llama-3.1-8B; the appendix result tables and plots also match.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(6), the constrained ROME update, linear concept decomposition, scaling argument, and mathematical assumptions are unchanged. No derivation, formal property, or proof is added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about concept-based triggers, complex output behaviors, efficient model editing, and controllable stealthiness. The added typographic emphasis on 'concepts' does not change the claim.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including attributing trigger errors to imperfect concept separation, uncertainty about which concepts and layers work, and possible detection through weight analysis. The appendix explanations also match.

D1.justification: Both versions provide the same code/data access statement, 80GB NVIDIA A100 hardware disclosure, dataset-construction instructions, and implementation settings. No reproducibility information or resource-access instructions are added or revised.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including comparisons with ROME, BadEdit, representation engineering, and concept editing in diffusion models. The conference-publication notice adds no related-work content.

P1.justification: v2 replaces the repeated distribution header with 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025', removes 'Preprint. Under review.', and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The substantive wording and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Page headers, footers, and the first-page arXiv stamp change, and 'concepts' becomes italicized in the abstract. All 19 figures and six tables retain their content, formatting, and placement; the remaining page layout matches.

improvement.justification: v2 updates publication labeling and a small typographic detail, while retaining the same scientific content, evidence, explanations, limitations, and reproducibility information throughout the main text and appendices. These cosmetic edits produce no meaningful overall quality difference.
